item: Overnight observation stay (CMS OPPS C-APC 8011) -- price sourced, NOT wired into the base case, see note
description: Comprehensive Observation Services, national base payment rate (wage-index UNADJUSTED), a bundled/packaged rate for a qualifying >=8-hour outpatient observation encounter -- not a per-mg or per-unit drug price like the rows above. payment_limit_usd_per_unit here is CMS's own CY2026 Addendum A figure ($2,672.15, RW 29.2310, SI J2) -- user-supplied 2026-08-05, and independently re-verified the same day by reading the primary source files directly (january_2026_web_addendum_a.12.29.25.zip's own APC 8011 row: Comprehensive Observation Services, SI J2, RW 29.2310, Payment Rate $2,672.15, exact match) -- this exactly reproduces (to the cent) against the $91.415 CY2026 conversion factor independently back-calculated the same day from the companion Addendum B file (29.2310 x 91.415 = 2672.15), a strong cross-validation between two CMS primary sources, now confirmed from the files themselves rather than a transcription of them. Historical trend for context: $2,174.14 (CY2016), $2,349.66 (CY2018), $2,283.16 (CY2021), $2,439.02 (CY2023), all from independent secondary sources citing the CMS OPPS final rule. R/04_costs_utilities.R's treg_dose_cost() takes this as an explicit opt-in observation_stay_cost_usd argument (default 0) rather than a base-case value -- not because the price is uncertain (it isn't, any more), but because whether a Treg infusion actually qualifies for C-APC 8011's billing criteria at all is a separate, still-open clinical/modelling question; see that module's header for the full reasoning and the wage-index caveat.
source: CMS's own "January 2026 Web Addendum A.12.29.25" (OPPS APCs for CY 2026), user-supplied 2026-08-05, APC 8011 row (Comprehensive Observation Services, RW 29.2310, Payment Rate $2,672.15); cross-validated against CMS's own "2026 January Web Addendum B.12.29.25" (companion file, same upload session) via its independently back-calculated $91.415 conversion factor. Historical rates (CY2016-2023) via RACmonitor (R. Hirsch, "Warning: Medicare Rates Up in 2023") and the ACEP reimbursement FAQ, both citing the CMS OPPS final rule.

item: UST maintenance (biosimilar-era, base case -- DERIVED PROXY, see note)
description: DERIVED PROXY, not directly observed: as of the April 2026 fee schedule, J3357 (ustekinumab SC/maintenance) no longer carries a Part B ASP payment limit at all (delisted from the file this project already sources from -- confirmed by its absence, not an extraction gap), which independently confirms the exact benefit-routing nuance flagged when this fix was scoped: self-administered SC maintenance dosing is not really a Part B ASP product, the same reasoning that already put ADA on a NADAC basis instead of ASP (see the ADA rows below). Unlike ADA, however, CMS's NADAC file does not yet carry ANY ustekinumab biosimilar NDC as of this pull (only brand STELARA: NADAC observed ~$29,798/mL, i.e. ~$331/mg, implausibly close to list and clearly not yet reflecting biosimilar substitution -- queried 2026-08-05, data.medicaid.gov dataset fbb83258-11c7-47f5-8b18-5f8e79f7e704, 'LIKE %STELARA%'/'LIKE %USTEKINUMAB-%' both checked). Absent a direct SC biosimilar reimbursement figure from either ASP or NADAC, this row applies the IV/induction biosimilar:originator ASP discount ratio found above (4.5375 / 11.624 = 0.390356, i.e. a 60.96% cut) to this project's own most recently sourced SC originator ASP figure (the row below, $155.883/mg, April 2025) -- 155.883 x 0.390356 = 60.8499. This assumes the SAME manufacturers' biosimilar competition discounts the SC formulation by roughly the same proportion as the IV formulation; that is a documented approximation, not an independently observed SC price, and should be revisited once NADAC (or a future ASP file) actually lists ustekinumab biosimilar SC NDCs.
